text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The wife of a Russian astronaut onboard the crippled space station Mir, Larisa Tsibliyeva, says her husband, as well as the other cosmonauts, are well-trained to tackle emergencies.

- Sergei Belyayev, head of the pro-government Our Home is Russia party in the Duma, says leading party member General Lev Rokhlin's outspoken appeal to President Boris Yeltsin is a reaction to the latest dismissals in the defence ministry.
- Russians will try to repair the dented space station Mir as soon as the cargo vessel, due for launch in 12 days, delivers an emergency repair kit to cosmonauts on board.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's visit to the United States has shown that American businessmen are extremely interested in doing business with Russia.
- Russia will use the latest $800 million credit from the World Bank to finance welfare reform.
- Russian aluminium smelters boycott Ukrainian alumina producers.
- Commercial banks urge the Central Bank to raise its refinancing rate.
SEVODNYA
- Elections of the governor of the Nizhny Novgorod region, a test-bed of economic reforms, will show whether fresh-faced reformers in the government still have a strong following in the region.
- Russian space station Mir will remain operational only for as long as there are cosmonauts on board.
- Russian power monopoly Unified Energy Systems is planning large-scale energy exports.
- Vasily Barchuk, head of Russia's state pension fund, favours a gradual reform of the pension system.
- Oil-producing joint ventures in Russia increase output.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russian borderguards open fire on a Japanese fishing boat three days after the Denver summit.
- The government pays back its debts to pensioners.
- Leaders of Tajik warring sides come to Moscow to sign a cooperation agreement but it is not clear whether the document will pave the way to a lasting peace in the war-torn republic.
- Russia keeps interfering in Afghanistan's internal affairs, says Islamic Taleban movement deputy foreign minister.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
